Mantle cell lymphoma. Mantle cell lymphoma is a rare, ag- gressive lymphoma of B-cell origin. Patients are often eld- erly and more often male. Most patients present with ad- vanced stage disease. Clinical features include fever, weight loss, drenching night sweats, and gastrointestinal symptoms.1 There is no established standard of care for mantle cell lymphoma.2 For the few patients presenting with localised disease, radiotherapy significantly improves progression- free survival, and is recommended first-line, with or with- out chemotherapy.1,2 Systemic combination chemothera- py, although non-curative, is recommended in advanced disease.1,2 Rituximab plus chemotherapy is recommended first-line.1-3 Chemotherapy options
